sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Nachshon of Yehudah represents self-nullification (bittul) and Nesanel of Yissachar represents Torah, with bittul being the vessel for Torah and preceding it in rank.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the discourses,
that the connection of Nachshon and Nesanel to Yehudah and Yissachar is,
that Yehudah is the matter of bittul (self-nullification)
[therefore he is called by the name Yehudah, from the phrase "This time I will thank (odeh) the L-rd"],
and therefore the prince of the tribe of Yehudah was Nachshon, who first descended into the stormy waves of the sea,
the matter of mesiras nefesh (self-sacrifice),
bittul.
And Yissachar is the matter of Torah
(as above).
And therefore the prince of Yissachar was Nesanel,
the letters of "Nasan Kel" (G-d gave),
for the Torah is a gift.
And the matter of Ben Tzuar,
Tzuar from the term "mitz'ar" (diminutive/small),
is,
that the vessel for Torah is bittul.
And this is that Yehudah brought an offering before Yissachar,
for the matter of bittul
is before
(and above)
the occupation with Torah.
For the root of Torah is in Chochmah (Wisdom),
for "the Torah emanates from Chochmah",
and through bittul there is a drawing down of Kesser (Crown) which is above Chochmah.
And it is necessary to understand,
that according to what is explained in the discourses that Yehudah is in Kesser and Yissachar is in Chochmah,
why did Scripture credit Yissachar as if he brought an offering first
(first also before Yehudah).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yehudah represents action and Yissachar represents study, and just as at the Giving of the Torah "Naaseh" (action) preceded "Nishma" (understanding), so too at the Chanukas HaMishkan Yehudah (action) preceded Yissachar (study).

translations.translation: And behold, it is known that Yehudah is the matter of action
(as stated in the discourses that explain the matter of the presentation of Yehudah and Yosef),
and according to this,
Yissachar and Yehudah are the matters of study and action.
And it is explained elsewhere
that although they counted and concluded that "study is greater",
nevertheless,
since the reason that study is greater is because study leads to action,
behold from this itself it is proven that action is the main thing
[for the root of action is above the root of study, and therefore in the future action will be greater].
And according to this it can be said,
that this [matter] that Scripture credited the prince of Yissachar as if he brought an offering first
(first also before Yehudah)
is in the manner of "study is greater",
and that in actuality Yehudah brought an offering first is because action is the main thing.
And to add,
the establishment of the Mishkan and the Giving of the Torah are related to each other.
And as is understood from the Midrashim of our Sages
on the verse
"I have come to My garden",
that the drawing down and descent of the essential Shechinah below to earth began at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
and the main drawing down was when the Mishkan was erected.
And according to this it can be said,
that just as the Giving of the Torah was through their having preceded "Naaseh" (we will do) to "Nishma" (we will hear),
emphasizing the superiority of action over study and understanding
("Nishma" from the term meaning understanding)
and in a manner that they preceded "Naaseh" to "Nishma"
[for after the Giving of the Torah,
although action is the main thing
and the reason that study is greater is because it leads to action, nevertheless study is greater,
and study precedes action.
But in order for the drawing down of the Giving of the Torah to be, there needed to be the preparation of the precedence of "Naaseh" to "Nishma"],
similarly is it regarding the drawing down that was at the erection of the Mishkan.
And therefore,
at the Chanukas HaMishkan, Yehudah brought an offering
(action)
before Yissachar
(study).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between "their end is wedged in their beginning" and "the end of the deed is in the initial thought," using the analogy of charity to show that the ultimate purpose is the actual deed and the recipient's reception, which is rooted in a level above the source of the influence.

translations.translation: And it is necessary to understand,
that since even this [matter] that study is greater is because it leads to action and action is the main thing,
what is the difference between the two matters,
that generally study precedes action
[precedes in time,
and also precedes in level,
"study is greater"],
and at the Giving of the Torah and likewise at the Chanukas HaMishkan action preceded.
And the point of the explanation in this is,
that this [matter] that action is the main thing
[even though action is the most external power,
and likewise Above action is the end of the chain of descent],
is because "their beginning is wedged in their end and their end in their beginning",
and also because "the end
of the deed is in the initial thought".
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
explains in the Hemshech TaRa"B,
the difference between the two matters,
that "their end" is the final conclusion of the drawing down.
And this level is wedged in "their beginning", the beginning and origin of the drawing down.
And as is brought there a parable for this from the giving of charity to a poor person,
that the beginning
(of the influence)
is that one is aroused with compassion for the poor person,
and from this there is generated within him afterwards a desire to benefit the poor person
[for compassion is the reason for the desire],
and afterwards the desire is drawn into intellect and emotions etc. until it comes into actual deed,
that he gives charity to the poor person.
And the matter of "their end is wedged in their beginning" is,
that the main intention in the arousal of compassion
(their beginning)
is that there be the actual influence
(their end).
And if there is no actual influence
[even though through the compassion there is generated the arousal of all his lofty powers,
desire, intellect and emotions,
and even when his desire to benefit the poor person is revealed in speech
(that he speaks words of appeasement to the poor person)
but does not come into actual deed],
the main thing is lacking.
And because "their end is wedged in their beginning",
that the intention
(the wedged [intention])
in the arousal of compassion
(their beginning)
is that there be the actual deed
(their end),
therefore "their beginning is wedged in their end",
that the revelation of the power of the aspect of beginning is
specifically at the end of the influence,
in the actual deed.
And the matter of "the end of the deed is in the initial thought" is above the matter of "their beginning is wedged in their end and their end in their beginning".
For the explanation of "the end of the deed" is
(not the end of the action itself,
the action of the person,
but rather)
the deed that comes about through the doing and action of the person.
For in the influence of kindness,
the matter of "the end of the deed" is the reception of the influence,
that the poor person receives the influence with goodness and enjoys from it.
For this matter
(in what manner the poor person receives the influence)
is not dependent on the giver but on the recipient.
And this reaches "in the initial thought",
i.e., in the beginning that is before the beginning of thought,
above the root of the influence.
For the root of the influence
(the arousal to bestow good)
is the beginning of thought,
and the revelation of this matter is at the end of the influence – "their beginning is wedged in their end",
and the level of "the end of the deed"
(the reception of the influence)
is that "the end of the deed" reaches the beginning that is before the beginning of thought,
above the root of the influence.
And therefore the pleasure that the influencer has from the reception of the influence
(from this that the poor person received the influence with goodness)
is a greater pleasure than the pleasure in the influence itself.
